newsitem.title: USA: Gore says only Israel-PLO can decide issues.
newsitem.headline: Gore says only Israel-PLO can decide issues.

text.p: Vice President Al Gore on Sunday night rebuffed a proposal by Israel's leader for the United States to enter its talks with the Palestinians, saying such a move would undermine peace efforts.

Addressing some 2,500 delegates attending a policy conference of the American Israel Public Affairs Committee, Gore spoke of the talks President Bill Clinton will hold on Monday with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in a bid to defuse the latest crisis that threatens to derail peace efforts.

Netanyahu proposed that all major issues that divide him and Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat be resolved within the next six months, and suggested that, if necessary, Clinton hold talks similar to the Camp David negotiations led by President Jimmy Carter.
"During this complex period, this administration will never let Israel down," Gore said to thunderous applause, telling the pro-Israel group, "I join you here as an ally."
He said three principles will guide Clinton as he seeks to revive peace efforts. The first, Gore said, is that "the issues in contention must not and cannot be resolved through violence."
Secondly, he said "issues must be resolved through direct give-and-take negotations between the parties involved. That is the only true path to success."

Saying that "the United States cannot and will not seek to impose its will upon either side," Gore said the third guideline would be to avoid allowing outside forces to influence the talks between the parties.

"Outside pressures will only be counterproductive and will only serve to undermine the peace process," Gore said. "Only the parties can determine the future of their people. ... We do not believe that Jerusalem or other permanent status issues are appropriate for others to decide."

In 1978 Carter separately held talks with the Egyptian and Israeli leaders before they were able to conclude the Camp David accords that paved the way for peace between the two Middle Eastern countries.
